title: A car losing value: an exponential model

stimulus.title: The value of a used car
stimulus.text: A used car loses value over time. Its value is $\$24{,}000$ one year after it was bought new and $\$14{,}500$ four years after it was bought. The value of the car, in dollars, is modeled by the function $C$ given by $C(t) = ab^t$, where $t$ is the number of years since the car was bought new.

table.caption: Value of the car, in dollars, t years after it was bought new

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ in the expression for $C(t)$.

accept: an equivalent pair, such as the ratio b^3 = 14500/24000 together with one of the equations

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the values of $a$ and $b$ as decimal approximations.

rubric.point: $a = 28389.581...$ and $b = 0.845...$ (both correct to three decimal places)
accept: values truncated to three decimal places

parts.sample: Dividing the equations: $b^3 = \frac{14{,}500}{24{,}000}$, so $b = \left(\frac{14{,}500}{24{,}000}\right)^{1/3} = 0.845381...$. Then $a = \frac{24{,}000}{b} = 28389.581350...$. Both are stored in the calculator.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $C$ over the interval $1 \le t \le 4$. Express your answer using correct units.

rubric.point: $-3166.667$ dollars per year, with the difference quotient and units

parts.sample: The average rate of change of $C$ on $[1, 4]$ is $\frac{C(4) - C(1)}{4 - 1} = \frac{14{,}500 - 24{,}000}{3} = -3166.667$ dollars per year.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the average rate of change from part B(i) to estimate the value of the car at $t = 3$ years. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: An estimate of $17666.667$ dollars from a point on the secant line through $(1, 24{,}000)$ and $(4, 14{,}500)$

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Is the estimate in part B(ii) an overestimate or an underestimate of $C(3)$? Give a reason for your answer, using the concavity of the graph of $C$ on the interval $1 \le t \le 4$.

accept: the estimate is greater than the model value C(3)

rubric.point: A reason from concavity on $[1, 4]$: $C$ is concave up there (decreasing, with its rate of change increasing), so the graph lies below the secant line
accept: "a > 0 and 0 < b < 1, so the graph of C is concave up on [1, 4]; the secant line lies above the graph, so the secant estimate is too large"
the average rates of change over equal intervals increase (become less negative), so C is concave up and the graph is below the secant line

parts.sample: Overestimate. On $[1, 4]$, $C(t) = ab^t$ with $a > 0$ and $0 < b < 1$, so $C$ is decreasing and concave up: the rate of change of $C$ is increasing. A concave-up graph lies below its secant line on the interval, so the point on the secant line at $t = 3$ is above the graph, and the estimate $17666.667$ is greater than $C(3) = 17152.039$.
